releases.author: github-actions[bot]
releases.description:
## What's new

- More organic, density-adaptive continents with finer irregular coastlines and variable sandy beaches.
- Solid globe mode now fully occludes the far hemisphere.
- Find searches both notes and tags.
- Selection details shows linked tags for selected notes.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Pavel-mik/obsidian-spherical-graph/compare/1.2.4...1.2.5
releases.name: Spherical Graph 1.2.5

releases.author: github-actions[bot]
releases.description: Continent detection now forms consensus candidates separately at coarse and fine CPM scales, recovering prominent hub-and-spoke and core/periphery communities that the former global consensus could miss. A conservative affinity pass completes clearly attached boundary notes, while a topology-cohesion gate continues to reject sparse chains. Isolated unassigned notes no longer punch lakes into supported land; accepted competing continents and coherent free-node groups still preserve sea. Use Renew layout to apply the revised detection and membership. The lake-rendering correction applies immediately. Verified with 40 test files / 196 tests, production-renderer browser QA on a 636-note graph, CI on Node.js 20, 22, and 24, release artifact validation, and build provenance attestation.

releases.author: github-actions[bot]
releases.description: Continent coastlines now follow the actual member cities and their short internal roads instead of filling a broad radial cap. Empty gaps and neighboring foreign or island cities carve visible sea, every accepted member seeds land, and long links cannot create implausible land bridges. This is a render-only correction: committed positions stay fixed and no Renew layout is required. Verified with 40 test files / 191 tests, production-renderer browser QA, CI on Node.js 20, 22, and 24, release artifact validation, and build provenance attestation.

releases.author: github-actions[bot]
releases.description:
Fixed large-vault continent detection: the automatic size threshold now grows sublinearly, and exceptionally stable regions with very few outward links can pass a guarded lower threshold. This restores compact, obvious continents without promoting sparse chains or returning to one land patch per free note.

Existing committed maps remain fixed after updating. Choose Map → Renew layout once to apply the revised continent classification.

Full changelog: https://github.com/Pavel-mik/obsidian-spherical-graph/compare/1.2.1...1.2.2

releases.author: github-actions[bot]
releases.description:
Fixed large-vault continent rendering: notes outside accepted continents now use a deterministic, density-aware island level of detail capped at 24 spatially separated land patches. Remaining notes stay fully interactive as cities over open water, preserving readable oceans without changing layouts, links, routes, or persistence.

Full changelog: https://github.com/Pavel-mik/obsidian-spherical-graph/compare/1.2.0...1.2.1

releases.author: github-actions[bot]
releases.description:
Spherical Graph 1.0.0 is the first stable desktop release.

Highlights:
- Seam-free fixed note layout computed intrinsically on a sphere.
- Explicit Initialize, Refresh, and Renew lifecycle with transactional persistence.
- Cyberpunk Three.js globe with tangent node markers, geodesic links, zoom-gated labels, and responsive selection details.
- All-shortest-route navigation with distinct endpoint and route highlighting.
- Selectable tag satellites on an adjustable orbit with occlusion and spiral links.
- Automatic Globe sizing, configurable appearance, search, clickable note details, and camera controls.

Privacy and security:
- No telemetry, ads, accounts, runtime network calls, remote code, external-file access, or note-content writes.

Manual installation: download `main.js`, `manifest.json`, and `styles.css` from this release into `<vault>/.obsidian/plugins/spherical-graph/`, then enable **Spherical Graph** in Obsidian.

See the [full changelog](https://github.com/Pavel-mik/obsidian-spherical-graph/blob/1.0.0/CHANGELOG.md) and [documentation](https://github.com/Pavel-mik/obsidian-spherical-graph#readme).
